Target: a nested case-control design

target_ncc.Rd

Builds the target of a nested case-control (matched case-control) study, in which each matched set holds one case and the controls sampled for it. The target sets the likelihood \(\ell(\theta)\) in the objective of cv.bregsurv(): the conditional log-likelihood of which member of each set is the case, $$\ell(\beta) = \sum_{m} \log \frac{\exp(z_{c(m)}^\top\beta)}{\sum_{j \in m} \exp(z_j^\top\beta)},$$ where \(c(m)\) is the case of set \(m\): the likelihood of a Cox model stratified by matched set.

target_ncc() checks your data and stores it; it fits nothing. Pass the result to cv.bregsurv() (or bregsurv()) as target.

Usage

target_ncc(case, set, z)

Arguments

case

Case indicator of each row: 1 for the case, 0 for a control. Coded as the event of target_cox().

set

The matched set of each row, any labels. Every set must contain exactly one case.

z

Covariates, one row per member of a set and one named column per covariate, as for target_cox().

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_target", a list with

type

"ncc".

case, set

The checked case indicators and matched sets.

z

The covariates as a numeric matrix with column names.

score

"linear".

n

The number of rows (members of all sets).

Details

A matched design has no follow-up time, so it takes no ties or stratum (the matched sets play the role of strata), and its risk score is always linear.

See also

cv.bregsurv(); the other targets, target_cox() and target_discrete(); the releases, release_records(), release_coef(), release_score() and release_model().

Examples

data(ExampleData_cc_lowdim)
cc <- ExampleData_cc_lowdim$train
target_ncc(case = cc$y, set = cc$stratum, z = cc$z)
#> Target: nested case-control design
#>   1000 subjects in 200 matched sets, 6 covariates
